title: Maximum Total Reward Using Operations II
summary: Given an integer array rewardValues, start with a total reward of 0 and no indices marked.
statement: Given an integer array rewardValues, start with a total reward of 0 and no indices marked. You can repeatedly choose an unmarked index i where rewardValues[i] exceeds the current total reward, add rewardValues[i] to the total reward, and mark index i. The goal is to determine the highest possible total reward achievable through optimal operations.
constraints: Start with total zero and use each index at most once.
A reward may be taken only when its value is strictly greater than the current total.
hints: Track reachable totals as set bits of one integer.
Before taking value v, only totals below v are eligible.
Mask those bits, shift them by v, and OR them into the reachable set.
Processing distinct values increasingly preserves every legal sequence and the highest set bit is the optimum.
editorial: Processing distinct values increasingly preserves every legal sequence and the highest set bit is the optimum.

tests.explanation: Take one then three to reach four; no remaining value exceeds four.
An optimal increasing-threshold order reaches eleven.
